history.period: Ancient; traditions claim very old origins (verify)
history.summary: Ancient shrine in the heart of Solan town dedicated to Goddess Shoolini, presiding deity of the former Baghat princely state. The city of Solan itself is said to be named after her (Solni → Shoolini → Solan). 'Shoolini' derives from Sanskrit 'shula' (spear); she is worshipped as a warrior form of Durga/Parvati, bearing the spear. Local legend also links her manifestation to the Sharabha myth (pacifying Vishnu's Narasimha). The annual 3-day Shoolini Mela (month of Ashadh, June) takes her palanquin through Solan to her sister's shrine (Shoolini Shakti Peeth) and back. No verified founding date exists; origins are preserved only in oral tradition.

name: Shoolini Mata Temple
town_description: Solan is a major town of Himachal Pradesh on NH-5 between Chandigarh and Shimla, and the headquarters of Solan district. It grew as a former British cantonment area and princely capital, and is known as the 'Mushroom City of India' for its horticultural research. It serves as the gateway town for Chail, Kasauli and the lower Shimla hills.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, ~70 km via NH-5
travel.railway: Solan railway station (Kalka-Shimla narrow-gauge line), ~2-3 km from the temple
travel.road: In the heart of Solan town on Jaunaji Road; well connected by bus/taxi from Chandigarh (~70 km) and Shimla (~44 km)

visitor_information.best_time: March to June (June for the Shoolini Mela) and September to November; avoid July-August monsoon
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): 5:00 AM-9:00 PM per one guide; 7:00 AM-6:00 PM per other travel sites; morning aarti ~6:00 AM, evening aarti ~7:00 PM
